task: Design-to-site pipeline: turn a flat design PNG into a REAL website -- a responsive, semantic page in normal flow, with the traced artwork as the hero backdrop and the copy as authored DOM. Design-agnostic -- three worked examples (A/B/C) remain as the TRACER's regression suite.
deliverable: a reusable PNG -> website pipeline packaged as a repo, plus a local studio (upload -> site). A/B/C are the tracer's regression suite: fixed 1024x768 POSTERS (layout: poster) scored on pixels exactly as before.
status: DONE and verified. A/B/C posters build clean and qa/verify.sh scores each real Astro dist/index.html (2.71 / 2.76 / 2.99 PASS). The studio builds a real responsive page end to end (doctor fixtures: light/montiva/antho PASS; doctor polarity PASS; doctor regress PASS). The generated page has a real visual design layer (type scale, sticky header with brand/nav/actions groups, hero scrim over a hero-band-cropped backdrop, section title rows, card grids, columns, alternating surfaces) and groups a name into one section however the reading order interleaves. A design review with gemini-3.1-pro was run twice against two real uploads; the ghosting it found first is fixed, and the composition defects it found second (hero crop, ghost CTA plate, header layout, flat cards, hero row order, stray badge section, contact panel hoisting, badge/button shape variance) are all fixed and guarded. Re-running qa/mkart.py from the committed PARAMS reproduces the shipped SVGs byte-for-byte (deterministic pipeline; the new blank_rects path is opt-in via the design config, so A/B/C are untouched).

north_star.what: image in -> real website out. The reference PNG is INPUT; the shipped page contains no raster image.
north_star.not: a pixel copy of the mockup. Pixel parity with the reference's TYPEFACE is deliberately not the target -- its residual was font substitution, which no sizing/weight/colour tuning removes.

two_measures.artwork: mean abs pixel diff over the ART REGION only (page-copy rects masked out) -- the tracer's job (studio/backend/app/verify.py). For a 'page' layout the art is scored by rendering the TRACED SVG alone at 1024x768, not by screenshotting the reflowing page (a page screenshot would measure layout, not tracing). A 'poster' (A/B/C) keeps scoring the page screenshot, which IS the artwork's frame.
two_measures.website: structure: landmarks, sections, one h1, resolving links, flow layout, reflow -- studio/backend/app/structure.py.

north_star.retired: the text-metrics layer: measure_lines, measure_weight, sample_line_colors, ink_coverage, per-line hard-stop gradients, glow tuning, cap_top_offset placement, width-solved font sizes.
north_star.kept: art colour sampling (sample_ink/sample_runs/sample_fill/sample_plate_fill/sample_contrast), refine_button_bbox/measure_button_bbox/snap_to_ink -- now only for the palette and the tracer's exclusion rects.

page_shapes.page: responsive semantic website, art as the hero backdrop via the <!--ART--> splice. Default for scaffolded designs and what the studio emits.
page_shapes.poster: the historical fixed 1024x768 stage. A/B/C use it, which is why qa/verify.sh still scores the traced art unchanged.

north_star.structure_merge: The vision model tags a section on EVERY block, so group_sections groups all blocks of a name into one section (a name is one section), ordered by position. Merging only ADJACENT runs was not enough: at a given y the reading order can interleave two sections (a testimonial's author line beside the contact band), which fragmented one section into several. A landing page with two feature bands keeps both bands inside one section and renders each as its own title+grid band. Without it a 75-block landing page shipped 75 <section> elements; with it, 3 (features/testimonials/contact) plus header/hero/footer. Guarded by `doctor polarity`.
north_star.design_layer: The generated page is more than extracted content: build_page_css emits a role-based type scale, a sticky header (brand left, nav centred, phone+button right -- three grid groups, not one flex row), a hero with the traced art under a directional scrim, section title rows with action links, card grids with hover, plain column bands, and alternating section surfaces (--card near-white with --shadow over a --tint band). palette() samples the reference's colours but enforces contrast (a design's headline can be a dark navy because it sat over a light hero panel; using it as body ink on a dark page made the whole page unreadable) and prefers the CTA's fill as the accent so buttons and highlights agree. Testimonials render as blockquote cards. Rows are emitted where they actually sit (a fine-print line drawn under the buttons stays under them); side-by-side buttons are ordered left-to-right (_row_order -- reading order sorts by top edge, which swaps a pair drawn two pixels apart). A one-line-item band renders as rules, not card chrome.
north_star.hero_band: The traced SVG is the WHOLE mockup, so splicing it whole puts the section below the hero into the backdrop -- the next section's cards and icons read as clutter behind the copy. generate.hero_band() computes the mockup's actual hero slice (top of the frame down to where the next section starts) and writes it to content.hero_band; gen-page.mjs narrows the spliced SVG's viewBox to it and uses preserveAspectRatio='xMidYMid slice'. The SVG FILE is untouched, so the art metric still renders the full artwork. Guarded by doctor polarity.
north_star.exclusion_rects: The tracer's exclusion rects are EVERY text block the model found -- the page copy that becomes DOM and the text inside the artwork (step callouts, a device mockup's own wordmark). Artwork-internal text is not emitted as DOM, but leaving it unblanked bakes a ghost of the word into the hero backdrop where the real copy sits, which is the ugliest defect the page can have. A text block is not art: it is blanked either way and mkart.py inpaints it from the surrounding pixels, so no hard hole appears. Guarded by doctor polarity ('exclusion rects cover artwork text').
north_star.blank_rects: A CTA button is a solid PLATE, and on a light ground the exclusion INPAINTS glyph ink rather than dropping luminance bands -- so blanking the label left the plate, ghosting under the DOM button ('an empty ghost button'). generate.button_rects() feeds mkart.build(blank_rects=...), rectangles removed wholesale. A button is chrome, never artwork. This is exclusion policy, not tracing math -- doctor regress confirms A/B/C are byte-identical.
north_star.studio_trace_point: generate.write_all pins the studio's trace params to bands=96, up=2 in the per-job designs/<id>.json. The newdesign.py scaffold default is 48, so the studio had been tracing every upload at HALF the resolution of the tuned A/B/C designs; 96 is a measured knee (48->96 improves the masked art mean on a real upload 4.244 -> 4.144; 192/384 are worse). The trace BOX stays the full frame: cropping it to the hero band measures worse (5.37 vs 4.14 at 96 bands) because mkart's band edges are percentiles of the box's own histogram, so a hero-only box re-bins the image against the hero's tonal range. hero_band still crops what is SHOWN (the viewBox), not what is traced. Studio-only: A/B/C's designs/*.json and params are untouched.
north_star.studio_nav_links: The vision model tags EVERY header/footer link `cta`, so a nav row (Home/Services/About) was indistinguishable from a real button (Book Service) and rendered as a stack of boxed buttons. generate._nav_cta_ids classifies a short cta in a row of >=3 short ctas as a nav link UNLESS it has a solid fill (the real button keeps its fill; nav links on a busy row come back outline=True with a contaminated fill). _cta_html emits class='navlink' for them; a run of them in a column is wrapped in .navlink-row so it flows horizontally. Nav-vs-button is a ROW-level decision needing BOTH shape and fill.
north_star.dark_ghosting_fixed: RESOLVED. On a DARK design with glowing COLORED type (AntHosting: green on near-black) the mockup's own headline was traced into the backdrop as a ghost behind the DOM copy -- the dark-path exclusion drops a band only when its median colour inside the rect exceeds text_lum_max (200), which assumes near-white type; a colored/dim fringe (lum ~105) never clears it. Fixed by reusing the LIGHT path's inpainting for dark designs too: generate.write_all now sends the text rects through blank_rects AND sets text_bg_lum to the design's ground for a dark background, so mkart finds ink by local contrast (polarity-agnostic) and fills it from the surroundings. The traced ghost disappears (u1 art 0.89->0.88, page whole 9.19->9.05). Ruled out by measurement: bigger exclusion rects and a per-rect local-background band-drop both made it worse. A/B/C never set text_bg_lum, so they stay byte-identical.
north_star.colour_blind_inpaint_fixed: RESOLVED. The light-path inpaint marked ink with |lum - bg_local| > 15, where lum is the MEAN of RGB, so a saturated colour near the ground was invisible: the anthotype wordmark's green 'type' (mean lum ~119 on a ~220 ground) was traced in full and its glow is the same green, so the stroke core read as background. mkart.build now marks ink by MAX-CHANNEL RGB distance against a PER-CHANNEL local background, and dilates 3*up instead of 2*up so the fill's nearest non-ink source is true background, not the glyph's own anti-aliased ring. The anthotype wordmark region goes to 0 green ghost pixels; the page whole mean drops 24.13 -> 19.16. Opt-in (text_bg_lum) so A/B/C are byte-identical.
north_star.hero_labels_not_copy: generate._drop_artwork_labels removes a hero illustration's own captions from the hero DOM. On the anthotype upload the model tagged EVERY block part:page, so the diagram's captions ('Generate', 'Time', 'Refine and grow meaning', a device-screen logo, the '1/2/3 Image/Sunlight/Plant Pigment' legend) became DOM paragraphs in the hero copy column. A short other/brand line that overlaps the headline/subhead band, or sits clear of the lede's right edge, is a caption, not copy. Drops 12 labels on anthotype, 0 on Montiva. The exclusion rects still use ALL blocks, so the labels are still blanked out of the traced art.
north_star.footer_nav_composition: generate._lift_bottom_nav moves a bottom-of-page nav-link run (tagged contact by the model because it sits under the contact band) into the footer. generate._footer_html renders the footer as a bar -- brand / footer-nav / footer-meta -- instead of a wall of equal-weight links.
north_star.known_limits: Icons (card icons, star rows, map pins) are artwork pixels, not DOM: a card's icon has no fixed position once the layout reflows, so recovering them as real assets is a separate feature. Artwork-internal labels are blanked along with the page copy (correct for the page, but it removes the illustration's own captions); keeping them re-introduces ghosting wherever a traced label lands behind DOM text, which is not known at trace time. The traced art is flatter than the mockup -- it is posterised into 24-26 luminance bands, the tracer's chosen payload/parity point.

metric: A/B/C posters: mean abs pixel diff over the 1024x768 stage vs the reference PNG (lower = closer). Studio pages: art-region pixel fidelity + a structural read of the built DOM (two measures, not one).
realistic_floor: ~3.0-3.4. The band-paint oracle beats the SVG render mainly on A and C because their bright bands are fragmented into 1-5px specks (78.9% of A bright ink, 57.2% of C) that vector tracing reproduces poorly; B is 26.0% and its oracle and render nearly agree. Raising `up` recovers this (A up=6 -> 3.67) at linear cost in file size.
breakthrough: the art layer is no longer hand-authored SVG shapes: it is real vector geometry recovered from the reference with potrace (qa/mkart.py), emitted through the normal page pipeline. Cut art error ~3-4x.

open_lead.summary: The art layer loses 5-8 of error between qa/mkart.py output and the browser.
evidence: the same bands emitted as SVG and rendered by Chrome score 7.3-10.1
open_lead.suspect: qa/mkart.py:_fmt() adds potrace's translate tx/ty to RELATIVE path deltas; a relative delta transforms as d*s with no offset. Verified by inspection.
open_lead.caution: respecting command case is correct SVG but drove the render white (mean lum 247 vs reference 16), so it interacts with something else -- likely the frame-plate subpaths or the translate(x0 y0) wrapper.

verified_fixes: qa/glyph.py:strip_frame_subpaths() -- potrace emits a frame-filling rectangle as the first subpath of a band; left in it painted an opaque black plate over the brand marks.
Stage radial-gradients double-counted glow already baked into the traced art. B .16/.10/.07 -> .02/.02/.03 alone took B 6.09 -> 5.01.
Art BOX widened to recover artwork the old box cut off (A's ring reaches x~363).
TEXT exclusion rects + text_lum_max=70 stop the trace baking a blurry copy of the DOM type under the real text, while keeping the dim glow behind it.
CSS_OVERRIDE='...' node gen-page.mjs <v> && ./qa.sh <v> is the reliable A/B path; qa/batch.py can disagree because it rebuilds from an older cached style block.
gotchas: potrace fills BLACK: pass the desired band as white; do not invert.
potrace emits its own y-flip translate(0,H) scale(1,-1); keep the transform, never rewrite coords.
qa.sh screenshots over file:// -- no server; a stray http.server once served stale art.
qa/batch.py._scope must be brace-aware or multi-line overrides are silently dropped.
Cap batch grids at COLS*MAX_ROWS or cells come back blank and scores go bogus.
gen-{a,b}.mjs are legacy hand-art generators; re-running them overwrites the good {v}.svg.
next_priorities: Payload vs parity is the one remaining dial on the posters: `bands` (~1 KB gzip per 0.001 mean). See qa/sweep_up.py.
Studio page quality: section grouping and copy come from a vision model plus clustering; the vision-critic review loop is still manual (see docs/AGENT-NOTES.md).
Icons (card icons, star rows, map pins) are artwork pixels, not DOM; recovering them as real assets is a separate feature.
Keep the gate green: `doctor gate` locally, .github/workflows/gate.yml in CI.
root_cause_fixed: potrace fills the BLACK/bit-0 region of a bitmap, and PIL's L->'1' conversion also writes the mask as bit 0, so qa/mkart.py was tracing the COMPLEMENT of every luminance band. The emitted frame-spanning plate painted an opaque near-black sheet over the whole art layer. The old _fmt() coordinate bug happened to shrink those plates into invisible slivers, which is why the page looked plausible while the art contributed ~0 -- verified: hiding .art changed the score by <0.01.
fix: qa/mkart.py passes (~mask)*255 to potrace and emits potrace's paths verbatim inside nested <g> transforms (no coordinate rewriting). _fmt() and the frame-plate stripper are both gone.
page_size_tradeoff: Measured Pareto (a): 2.77 @ 6.7MB, 2.85 @ 5.7MB (up3/bands64), 2.86 @ 4.3MB (up2/bands64), 2.94 @ 3.2MB (up2/bands48). (c): 3.11 @ 8.0MB, 3.24 @ 4.8MB (up2/bands64), 3.40 @ 2.8MB (up1/bands64). (b): 2.84 @ 4.8MB (up4/bands32), 2.90 @ 3.5MB (up4/bands24), 3.09 @ 1.9MB (up4/bands16). Shipped point is the best-value knee, not the max-parity extreme.
open_leads: TEXT is now the largest single contributor (a 1.47, b 1.75, c 1.77 of the overall mean, vs art 1.06/1.42/1.37) but is at a local optimum for the Inter stack. Only a different font or a higher-resolution reference could move it.
More bands still buys score (a 128 bands -> 2.75) at ~1 KB gzip per 0.001 mean -- a pure size/parity judgement, not a technical barrier.
B brand / C brand remain the worst regional means (small areas).
incremental_wins: CUMULATIVE BANDS: trace {lum >= e_i} instead of the disjoint band {e_i<=lum<e_{i+1}}. Mathematically identical painted darkest-first, but one solid nested region per band instead of scattered 1px slivers: a 3.76->2.99, b 3.36->3.23, c 3.78->3.32, and the SVG halves.
alphamax=0 + opttol=0: a 3.76->3.65, c 3.78->3.72, b 3.36->3.34; file smaller. opttol is inert; alphamax=1.0 makes files BIGGER, so flat polygons are optimal at these resolutions.
Operating point moved to the knee of the size curve: a up2/bands64, b up4/bands24, c up2/bands64.
resolved_leads: The _fmt() relative-coordinate lead is dead: cumulative masks removed the need for any coordinate rewriting and closed the art gap.
The A/C bright-band speck diagnosis is superseded: the loss was the disjoint-band decomposition, not the specks themselves.
exhausted_from_previous_session: FONT: Inter beats Inter Tight/Inter Display/SF Pro/Helvetica Neue/Archivo/Public Sans by ~1.3 mean on a and ~0.9 on c. Inter is correct.

TYPE METRICS: h1 font-size is centred at its optimum on all three (a 80, b 84, c 82 px); letter-spacing, font-weight, transform, ink colour and opacity all fail to improve it. Text is at its floor for this stack.
BLUR: 0 px is optimal for all three (0.5 px costs 0.04-0.27).
BAND EDGES: uniform binning beats quantile binning and 1-D k-medians, which over-weight the huge dark region (a 1.74 vs 1.77 vs 3.45 paint error).
opttol is inert; alphamax=1.0 makes files bigger, so flat polygons are optimal.
text-shadow / glow RE-CHECKED under the corrected scorer: NOT exhausted -- tightening radius/alpha gained 0.05-0.09 on every variant. See glow_fix.

reproducible: Verified: re-running qa/mkart.py from the committed PARAMS produced byte-identical {a,b,c}.svg to the shipped ones.
viewing: cd preview/ && ./start-persistent.sh 4173  ->  http://127.0.0.1:4173/ (gallery), /a/ /b/ /c/, /ref/<v>, /diff/<v>. Use start-persistent.sh (double-fork via daemonize.py) NOT `serve.py &` -- a background job dies with its shell, which is why the URLs previously stopped resolving. launchctl submit does not work (launchd cannot read the external volume). astro dev does NOT work on this project (managed dev server ignores --port; hangs re-transforming ~7MB inline SVG per request). The pages are self-contained and open directly from dist/index.html with no server and no network. Default browser is Safari.

self_hosted_fonts.what: Inter is vendored at pipeline/fonts/*.woff2 (6 weights, 144 KB) and inlined as @font-face by gen-page.mjs; the Google Fonts <link> and both preconnects were removed.
self_hosted_fonts.why: The page previously loaded Inter from the Google Fonts CDN, so its typography -- and the scored fidelity -- depended on the network. With fonts.googleapis.com + fonts.gstatic.com DNS-blackholed the old build scored 4.22 on A instead of 2.71 (silent fallback to Helvetica).
self_hosted_fonts.result: Offline score is identical to online.  Re-measured with the current scorer (PIL Lanczos) and the tightened glow it is 2.71 / 2.76 / 2.99, delta < 0.0001 mean vs the online render.
self_hosted_fonts.required_config: build.inlineStylesheets: 'always' in every astro.config.mjs. The font CSS pushes the stylesheet past Astro's 4 kB auto-inline threshold; without it Astro emits /_astro/index.*.css which cannot load over file:// -- the protocol qa.sh and qa/verify.sh screenshot with. Symptom of regression: scores jump to 158/170/227 and the page renders unstyled.
self_hosted_fonts.gate: qa/verify.sh fails on remote asset refs AND external /_astro/*.css, and asserts zero page-originated network requests via qa/netcheck.py (Chrome net-log based). qa/netcheck.py --selftest proves the detector sees a deliberate CDN fetch, so a zero is trustworthy. Both gates negative-tested.
self_hosted_fonts.payload_cost: 3 weights (400/500/600) only -- those are the only font-weight values used across the three page CSS files. 72 KB of woff2 inlined as base64. Base64 costs ~33% raw but gzip removes exactly that, so the gzip delta equals the raw font size (~72 KB/variant) and the page stays a single file with zero extra requests.
self_hosted_fonts.measured: Net-log verified: 0 page-originated http(s) requests on all three builds.

preview_persistence.problem: The preview server had been started as a background job from a shell that later exited, so it was killed and the URLs stopped resolving in the browser.
preview_persistence.fix: preview/start-persistent.sh uses preview/daemonize.py (double-fork + setsid) so the server is re-parented to launchd (PPID 1) and survives shell exit.
preview_persistence.note: launchctl submit does NOT work here -- launchd cannot read the external volume (Operation not permitted). The double-fork in daemonize.py is the working approach.

font_loading: self-hosted (was: Google Fonts CDN). See self_hosted_fonts.

non_pixel_fixes.artwork_a11y: The traced SVG was announced as aria-label='AntHosting {v} artwork', leaking the internal variant letter. Now aria-hidden='true' focusable='false' (the art is decorative). Geometry byte-identical; scores unchanged. Fixed in qa/mkart.py.
non_pixel_fixes.cta_dead_link: A/B/C POSTERS: the CTA is href='#waitlist' but no element with that id exists, so the button does nothing. Those are fixed posters (the tracer's regression suite), not a website. The STUDIO's generated pages no longer have this gap -- their CTAs point at a real in-page anchor. Set a real URL in the returned content-<id>.json.

scores_previous_scaler.note: produced with `sips -z`; the shipped scorer is now PIL Lanczos (qa/downsample.py)

scorer_downgrade_fixed.what: The 2x screenshot -> 1024x768 reference resize used `sips -z`, which is the worst measured reconstruction filter. PIL Lanczos is now canonical (qa/downsample.py), used by both qa.sh and qa/verify.sh.
scorer_downgrade_fixed.why_it_matters: The filter is not neutral: on B, sips 2.8970 vs lanczos 2.8205 -- 0.077, about 2.7% of the headline number. Page pixels were NOT changed to obtain this; only the measurement improved.
scorer_downgrade_fixed.targets: Tightened to 2.82 / 2.88 / 3.15 (~0.06 headroom above the stable value).

glow_fix.what: text-shadow radius/alpha tightened on h1, h1 .green and h2 across all three variants (h1 14-18px->8-10px; h1 .green 18-20px->6-10px and alpha .30-.32->.20-.22; h2 12px->6px).
glow_fix.why_it_was_missed: The previous session swept glow under the old `sips -z` scorer and concluded the shipped values were optimal. The blur introduced by that scaler hid the improvement. Re-swept via qa/tune.py against the corrected Lanczos scorer, it reproduces on all three.
glow_fix.gain: A 2.76->2.71, B 2.82->2.76, C 3.08->2.99. Stable +/-0.01 over 3 runs. pct>30 unchanged (1.13/1.59/1.57), so this is not a contrast trade.
glow_fix.lesson: Anything in the exhausted list that was judged only by aggregate mean should be re-checked now the scorer is honest. Font metrics were re-checked and still hold; glow did not.

adding_a_design.build: node gen-page.mjs <name> && node to-astro.mjs <name> && (cd ../sites/variant-<name> && npm install && npm run build)

adding_a_design.layout: newdesign.py scaffolds layout: 'page' -- a responsive website with the traced art as the hero backdrop (the <!--ART--> placeholder). Pass through design.layout='poster' only to keep the historical fixed 1024x768 stage (what A/B/C use).

verification.gate: studio/backend/doctor.py gate -- runs env -> polarity -> fixtures -> regress in order, fails if any stage fails. regress IS qa/verify.sh, so it covers both measures (A/B/C pixel fidelity + the fixtures' structure). --quick runs polarity alone (no potrace/node/Chrome/model).
verification.fixtures: doctor fixtures replays saved extractions (no model) and guards BOTH measures: structure (app.structure.inspect) AND the artwork's pixel fidelity via a per-fixture score_max on the art-region mean (light/antho 3.0, montiva 5.0; negative-tested). Fixture scores are not comparable between fixtures or to A/B/C.
verification.ci: .github/workflows/gate.yml -- gate --quick on every push/PR (macos-latest, seconds, no pipeline); the full gate on main and nightly after a from-source build.
verification.pinned_python: pipeline/requirements.txt and studio/backend/requirements.txt are PINNED on purpose: the scores are a numeric gate computed through numpy/scipy/scikit-image/PIL, so an unpinned pip install could move a score with no code change. Bump deliberately and re-record the numbers.
verification.docs_consistency: doctor regress parses the qa/verify.sh means and fails if STATE.json scores/targets no longer match designs/*.json and the run, so this file cannot silently drift. When a target changes, update it here in the same commit.
verification.critique: doctor critique <job-id | design.png> screenshots the built page and asks the vision model to review it against the mockup, printing a ranked list of composition/readability defects (typeface differences excluded). --page reviews an existing page, --out saves the report. A review tool, NOT a gate stage: it needs a live model and is subjective.
